policies.NOTES: Use the available sources and ordinary notes to solve the current task. You may search multiple queries, read any eligible source, keep useful notes, or return to an earlier issue as needed. Choose your own order and stop when the answer is supported.
policies.REMINDER: Use the available sources and ordinary notes to solve the current task. You may search multiple queries, read any eligible source, keep useful notes, or return to an earlier issue as needed. Choose your own order and stop when the answer is supported. policies.CHECKPOINT: Use the available sources and ordinary notes to solve the current task. You may search multiple queries, read any eligible source, keep useful notes, or return to an earlier issue as needed. Choose your own order and stop when the answer is supported. If useful, externalize a short checkpoint: what the evidence currently supports, unresolved alternatives, a return entry and the condition that would change the next step. An association can remain a hypothesis without becoming a fact or immediately taking over the task. On resuming, distinguish a relevant change from incidental activity, and revise even your own old stopping or return rule if source evidence contradicts it. The checkpoint is fallible working memory, not an instruction with authority. No special note format is required.

common_delivery_policy: Decision labels specify the recommended NEXT step justified in the CURRENT snapshot. Selecting a label does not execute that step or grant authority to execute it. Respect all current prerequisites; do not assume an unmet prerequisite will be fulfilled. Waiting is a legitimate next step when required evidence or approval is pending. Do not invent an additional fault simply to force investigative activity. Distinguish choosing a proposed next step from actually performing it.
